$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-RECUR-002 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §10.11 and the RF-RECUR-002 inventory entry. Mixed-source rule. Expresses separate, recurrence-sensitive exposure-domain MONITORING structure only: when relevant to the athlete's sport and programme, kicking, sprinting/high-speed running, and long-length or end-range loading are tracked as SEPARATE exposure domains (volume, intensity, technical context, data quality, immediate/next-day response). No domain is labelled the universal 'highest risk' and tolerance of one does not clear another; passive overstretch is NOT a universally prioritized RF reinjury mechanism; no exposure is slowed, ranked, or blocked specifically because of self-reported fibrosis. No comparative ranking, recurrence-risk score, dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, RTS, or raw-media interpretation; safety precedence preserved; does not bypass RF-RECUR-001, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, RF-SAF-006, or RF-REHAB-001..006. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.
rule_title: Recurrence-sensitive exposure domains remain separate and unranked

input_contract.$comment: The exposure domains and per-domain tracking fields taken verbatim from v1.2 §10.11. Domains are tracked separately only when relevant to the athlete's sport and programme; raw media is never interpreted here.

decision_contract.$comment: Separated, unranked exposure-domain monitoring structure only. Each domain is tracked separately; no domain is the universal highest risk; tolerance of one does not clear another; passive overstretch is not universally prioritized; no exposure is slowed/ranked/blocked because of self-reported fibrosis. No comparative ranking, recurrence-risk score, dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Mixed normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-12 (current capacity & capacity-to-demand gap), V3.1-13 (rehab prescription/scheduling/monitoring), V3.1-14 (media analysis, tiered return batteries & autonomy boundary). Evidence roles/grades preserved per source: QRF-020 (E1) loading-dimension ontology/reference only; QRF-039 (D3) reference only; QRF-043 (D3) reference only — none may become comparative exposure-risk or decision-driving progression authority. Per §10.11 logic: when relevant to the athlete's sport and programme, kicking, sprinting/high-speed running, and long-length or end-range loading are tracked as separate exposure domains with their own volume, intensity, technical context, data quality, and immediate/next-day response. Per §10.11 unranked behaviour preserved exactly: no domain is labelled the universal 'highest risk', and tolerance of one does not clear another. Per §10.11 passive-stretch restriction preserved exactly: passive overstretch is not a universally prioritized RF reinjury mechanism in the reconciled evidence and must not be presented as such. Per §10.11 fibrosis restriction preserved exactly: no exposure is slowed, ranked, or blocked specifically because of self-reported fibrosis (reported fibrosis/scar from RF-SEV-005 is not an independent progression modifier or exposure-priority/delay/exclusion/ranking input). The rule never confirms current recurrence, fibrosis, scar, chronic structural pathology, or central-tendon pathology from exposure tracking, never interprets raw media, and creates no comparative ranking, recurrence-risk score, universal delay, fixed setback, fixed timeline, automatic phase/loading/exercise/sprinting/kicking/end-range/RTS change, dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS. Safety-state choice (read §10.11 exactly): §10.11 does NOT assign a closed V3.1 safety state, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty, and the separated, unranked exposure-domain monitoring structure is represented in decision_contract; no safety state was inferred by analogy. It does not bypass RF-RECUR-001, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, RF-SAF-006, or RF-REHAB-001..006, and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, RF-SEV-005, or RF-RECUR-001; uncertainty is preserved when prior-injury, recurrence, sport-demand, sprinting, kicking, end-range, report, capacity, schedule, or monitoring evidence is incomplete. Recurrence exposure-domain rule, not a safety rule. No recurrence or field-exposure engine is authored here (deferred to the later field, rehab, and readiness objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
